guide: Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: close target, margin floor, loaded labour rates, diagnostic fee, member discount and financing factor.
Check Job Types and Labour Rates. They hold your target margin by job type and the labour cost the price book uses.
Fill Parts Cost List with today's supplier cost. Every price book line reads its parts cost and its main part from there.
Keep the Price Book up to date: hours, parts, permit, disposal, subcontract and flat price. Cost, margin, the gap to target and the price needed fill in by themselves.
Log every supplier cost change on Supplier Price Changes, then read Lines Under Target to see which lines need a new price.
Add every estimate to Estimates with its three prices, the option chosen, the outcome and the follow-up date. Open Estimates ranks what to call first.
Use Option Builder for good, better and best lines with margin and a monthly payment from your financing factor.
Read Close Rate by Option, Technician and Job Type, Lost Reasons and Estimates by Month to see where estimates are won and lost.
Type each month of diagnostic visits on Diagnostic Visits and log phone quotes on Quote Log.
Use the 18 tools for line prices, margin checks, supplier changes, options, follow-ups, price reviews, fees and financing.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
A one-person owner-operator with one van can use the Price Book as a quote sheet; a shop with a dispatcher shares the follow-up list with the office.
Read the KPI Dashboard and Charts every week: close rate, money on the table, margin lines under target, lost value and diagnostic conversion.

listing.title: HVAC and Plumbing Price Book Excel Template: Flat-Rate Pricing, Estimates, Good-Better-Best Options, Margin and Follow-up
listing.headline: Price every job from cost and win more of your estimates
listing.description:
Run the pricing and estimates side of an HVAC and plumbing business in one Excel workbook. Built for a small owner-run service shop with 1 to 15 technicians, or a one-person owner-operator who uses the price book as a quote sheet.

The Price Book holds a flat-rate price for each task, a fixed price built from cost: labour hours at your loaded rate, parts, permit, disposal, subcontract work and the trip. Cost, margin, the gap to your target margin, the price needed and the money lost a year on each line fill in by themselves. Supplier Price Changes and Parts Cost List show which lines fall under target after a supplier price rise, and Lines Under Target ranks them.

Estimates records every estimate with good, better and best prices (three priced options for one job), the option chosen, the outcome and the follow-up date. Open Estimates ranks what to call first, and Option Builder shows margin and a monthly payment from a financing factor you enter. Close Rate by Option, Technician and Job Type compare the last 90 days, the last 12 months and the year before; Lost Reasons and Estimates by Month show where money is lost.

18 tools answer weekly questions: the price at your margin target, supplier price impact, the option to lead with, estimate follow-up, the yearly price review, the price rise break-even, the diagnostic fee test, member prices, financing and phone quotes. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to customers, landlord accounts, technicians, suppliers and your accountant.

This is part two of the HVAC and Plumbing Contractor suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data. It helps you keep track of prices and estimates and does not promise results.
